newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: UNISYS SAYS MULLING FURTHER APPEAL IN CZECH TENDER.
newsitem.headline: UNISYS SAYS MULLING FURTHER APPEAL IN CZECH TENDER.

text.p: U.S.-based Unisys Corp said on Friday it is considering its third appeal of a Defence Ministry decision awarding an army contract to a consortium of Electronic Data Systems and Digital Equipment Corp.

Late on Thursday, the Czech Economic Competition Office rejected an April appeal by Unisys and IBM over the tender results, which followed a first round appeal denial by Defense Minister Miloslav Vyborny.
"We have received a letter from the Competition Office on the decision," Ales Benda, a spokesman for the firm told Reuters on Friday.

"The decision of the Competition Office could be appealed within 15 days. We are studying the reasons and the documents which we have received and reserve the right to appeal this decision," he added.
IBM officials were not immediately available for comment.
Benda said Competition Office chief Stanislav Belehradek would hear the appeal if it is launched, and added that Unisys could also appeal directly to a Czech court if it wishes.

Vyborny rejected the first round appeal by Unisys and IBM Corp saying he believed his decision in March to award a 1.3 billion crown army information system deal to EDS-Digital was correct. Vyborny chose EDS-Digital despite a recommendation by a steering committee to chose Unisys's bid.

Vyborny said that he decided in favour of EDS-Digital due to the lower price of its bid. Unisys has said that price was not weighted in accordance with the tender rules, and that EDS-Digital's offer was not complete. EDS declined to comment.
Unisys won an original four billion crown supply tender last year, but it was cancelled in August when competition authorities found irregularities in the process.

Vyborny said after the second tender that the ministry had also decided to ignore the recommendation of the tender committee because some members' evaluations significantly differed from the rest of the committee.
Unisys has said it was suspicious that the original tender was abolished and rankings were changed when it won again.
A number of other Czech military tenders have been marked by controversy, sometimes including allegations of corruption.
Installation of the staff information system is seen as a large step on the Czech army's path to compatibility with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's military command.

NATO leaders will officially decide in July which former communist countries will be invited to join the alliance. The Czech Republic along with Poland and Hungary were named by the U.S. on Thursday as its choices for expansion.
